correctness.rationale: Exact Fourier correlation identities yield a partial character on the nonzero support. Graph connectivity for each \(N-2r>2r\) overlap and a nonempty \(N-3r\) triple overlap produce an actual character extension, hence a translate. At sharpness, all six unordered zero-sum Fourier triples on \(\mathbb Z_8\) have exact product phase one; DC dominance proves strict positivity. Product families preserve zeros/correlations. Standalone numerical and exact integer checks corroborate but are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: Third-order bispectrum phase recovery under adversarial Fourier erasures has a natural universal threshold question. The result determines the exact sharp erasure fraction one-quarter across all finite abelian groups, identifies the structural mechanism by a dense partial-character lemma, and exhibits strictly positive sharpness examples for arbitrarily large groups. The identification and exact boundary have direct mathematical significance beyond a finite experiment.
